extraction: VizieR ASU TSV export, -out=**&-out.max=unlimited. Cleaned file maps upstream columns to a standard schema (id,ra_deg,dec_deg,z,z_err,q_flag,member_flag) and appends sep_arcmin and R_proj_Mpc computed from the cluster centre with FlatLambdaCDM(H0=70,Om0=0.3). No rows dropped. Where the upstream redshift is stored as a velocity cz in km/s it is converted to z=cz/c and its uncertainty is converted consistently to dz=e_cz/c; otherwise no values are altered. Raw upstream response kept verbatim in raw/.
note: MACS J1149.5+2223 (z=0.542). Grillo, Karman, Suyu, Rosati, Balestra, Mercurio et al. 2016, ApJ 822, 78, table 1 'MUSE spectroscopic catalog'. 134 rows, of which 129 carry a redshift. Quality: column QF (0-9); column EL flags emission-line objects; zlit gives literature comparison redshifts. Coordinates are SEXAGESIMAL upstream and were converted to decimal degrees. Instrument: VLT/MUSE, a single ~1 arcmin pointing centred on the SN Refsdal host. Selection function: everything detected in the single MUSE datacube. SEVERE LIMITATION: sky coverage reaches only ~0.7 arcmin (~0.28 Mpc projected) and only ~74 objects lie within |dv|<3000 km/s. This is far too few, over far too small a radial range, to build a sigma(R) field. Note table 6 of the same paper lists 300 candidate cluster members but is PHOTOMETRIC (no redshifts) and was therefore not acquired.
